text:
maria: Heads up — seeing repeated tail-latency spikes on eu-west-1 dedicated pool 'pool-A' starting ~10:12 UTC. A bunch of customers pinned to that pool are seeing degraded p99s. GPU util ~98% but host CPU/mem look fine. Suspect noisy neighbor (large KV/cache churn).

infra-bot: ALERT: pool-A gpu0 gpu1 utilization >95% | p99 latency 450ms | 10:12:08 UTC

sam: Thanks Maria. Can you paste the stack of affected tenants and model sizes? Any single pod using >1 model or long seq lengths?

maria: quick snapshot:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-pool-A top pods --containers
NAME                      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)   GPU
tenant-x-encoder-0        2m           1.2Gi           1/1
tenant-y-infer-0          50m          2.5Gi           1/1
tenant-z-chat-0           10m          1.1Gi           1/1
```
logs show repeated KV cache evictions and large prefix hits from tenant-y: many long-context requests (~8k tokens) and model pinned to fp16 variant.

devon: That sounds like cache churn. Pool-A is mixed-tenancy (ML-std nodes + a couple of high-mem L40s). If tenant-y is doing large seqs, it'll thrash the shared KV cache and raise GPU memory pressure.

raj: Options: emergency isolation to a dedicated mini-pool for tenant-y, reduce allowed seq length for noisy tenants, or enable per-tenant KV partitioning (harder). What is the cost delta for spinning up a small dedicated node?

laura: Quick cost calc: a single L40 reserved on-demand in eu-west-1 is ~3.6 USD/hr (spot cheaper but unstable). For 12h that’s ~43 USD. Versus p99 regressions costing SLA credits and poor UX.

sam: Can we reroute tenant-y to our 'burst-dedicated' capacity in eu-west-1 temporarily? That pool has capacity but routing policy currently prefers cost tiers.

maria: Tried manual reroute with staging flag, got a fail: "no compatible endpoint in eu-west-1 with enough memory". I think our routing constraint table still disallows burst-dedicated for customers on reserved-dedicated contracts unless operator overrides.

devon: That routing rule exists to honor isolation tiers. We can temporarily override via the operator console: set route.policy for tenant-y -> allow_burst=true. But need approval for customers under reserved SLAs.

raj: If we do that, we must ensure no data isolation breaches. Burst-dedicated is still single-tenant for the served workload, right? It’s not mixed.

laura: Yes burst-dedicated is single-tenant but hosted in same AZ. KMS keys stay customer-specific. Security ok.

sam: Ok Maria — can you try operator override? Steps:
1) curl -X POST "$CONSOLE/api/v1/operators/reroute" -d '{"tenant":"tenant-y","target_pool":"burst-dedicated-eu-west-1","reason":"noisy-neighbor emergency"}'
2) watch logs and verify model warms on target

maria: Running now.
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/operators/reroute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"tenant-y","target_pool":"burst-dedicated-eu-west-1","reason":"noisy-neighbor emergency"}'
```

infra-bot: Operator action recorded: reroute requested by maria at 10:21:53 UTC (event id: evt-23f7)

maria: Reroute accepted by control plane but the scheduler can't find a matching node: "no nodes with >48GB free GPU memory and compatible kernel." Looks like burst-dedicated had 1 node but it's hosting onboarding jobs.

devon: We can preempt one onboarding job (non-critical) to free up an L40. Suggest sending eviction with 10m grace.

sam: Approve preempt. Maria, evict command?

maria: Issuing eviction now: `kubectl delete pod onboarding-ml-rcv --grace-period=600 -n burst-dedicated`

infra-bot: Preemption scheduled: onboarding-ml-rcv will be evicted in 600s.

maria: Tenant-y model is warming on target pool. GPU mem footprint ok. Initial p99 dropping to ~110ms within warmup.

laura: Good. For medium-term: we should consider adding soft isolation knobs to Dedicated: either guaranteed KV partitions per tenant, or strict tenant-affinity where certain noisy tenants live on dedicated hosts. Both increase cost.

raj: Proposal for follow-up doc:
- Detection: better noisy-neighbor detection (KV eviction rate, long-context token ratio)
- Mitigation: automatic reroute to burst-dedicated or temporary per-tenant node assignment
- Policy: cost/accounting changes for emergency shifts (bill back to tenant when using dedicated spare capacity)
- Long term infra: inventory pools by seq-length workload and create L40-heavy pools for long-context models

devon: Also engineering task: support per-pool KV namespace isolation. We can implement namespace ids in runtime and keep separate caches. Complexity: increased memory overhead + scheduler matching.

sam: Add evaluation of enabling `nvidia-mps` or multi-process service to reduce contention? However for LLM MPS doesn't help with KV cache thrash — it's mostly GPU memory evictions.

maria: Agreed. Short-term action list we completed:
- evicted onboarding job to free node (10:30 UTC)
- rerouted tenant-y to burst-dedicated (10:33 UTC)
- p99 for affected customers down from 450ms -> ~120ms (10:37 UTC)

laura: Can finance model the cost impact of keeping a 1-node warm buffer per region for burst-dedicated? Estimate: 24/7 L40 reserved = 3.6 * 24 * 30 ~ 2592 USD/mo per region. Maybe we do shared buffer across adjacent regions?

raj: Shared buffer cross-region adds latency/egress costs though. Need SLO analysis.

devon: For immediate follow-up, I'll open infra ticket to prototype per-tenant KV namespaces on runtime and a scheduler label to pin long-context tenants.

maria: Also documenting routing override recipe in runbook (so oncall can do this without infra pager). Will paste link when done.

sam: Nice work everyone. Please update the incident tag and mark as mitigated once runbook link is in thread.

maria: Runbook draft: https://wiki.internal/redwood/infra/noisy-neighbor-dedicated-pools - added (WIP). Marking mitigated for now; keeping monitoring for 2h. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INCIDENT: noisy-neighbor-eu-west-1 -> mitigated by operator reroute (evt-23f7). Monitoring window: 2h.

laura: We'll sync tomorrow to decide reserve vs on-demand burst budget.

maria: Thanks all, closing thread unless new regressions appear.
